solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: It's back to the accounts book to write in 'Paid'

indicators.note: back tells us the word its is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: the word its, ignoring the apostrophe
a pen is what you write in ink with, so the phrase gives the instrument
a diary is a book in which daily matters and accounts are recorded

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go back to the ledger and enter a payment as made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses ITS; 'Paid' is the definition in the sense of salaried, as a stipendiary magistrate is paid rather than voluntary.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipendiary magistrate or clergyman receives a regular salary, so the adjective means salaried.

clue.text: Scrabble piece that gets fifty in game

indicators.note: in places the fifty within the word for a game

parts.note: a tie is a sports match or fixture, as in a cup tie
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A Scrabble player lays a piece that scores fifty points.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts L inside TIE; a cup TIE is a knockout match in British football.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble letters are printed on small square tiles, so one piece is a tile.

clue.text: Guide dog?

definitions.meaning: something that indicates direction, like an arrow on a dial
a breed of gun dog that stands still and aims its nose at game

explanation.definitionFit: A pointer is both an indicator that guides the eye and a breed of hunting dog.

clue.text: Unknown child turned up with lots of questions

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word for child is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a son is a male child
Y is one of the algebra letters used for an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: An unidentified youngster appears, firing off endless questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses SON to NOS, then the unknown Y is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A nosy person is inquisitive, always asking questions about others' business.

clue.text: Lizards that may be using a double disguise

indicators.note: disguise means the letters are given a new appearance by rearranging them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: double here means the single letter a is to be written twice over

explanation.surface: Lizards might wear a two-layer camouflage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguise' rearranges USING plus AA; 'may be' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Iguanas are large tropical American lizards, so the plural fits the plural definition.

clue.text: It flies or takes a train

definitions.meaning: a marsh bird of the family that includes the corncrake
travels by railway, the verb sense

explanation.definitionFit: Rail is the name of a wading bird, and to rail is to travel by train.

clue.text: Unsteadiness shown when sick during holiday

indicators.note: during places the word for sick within the period of the holiday

parts.note: a vacation is a holiday
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A traveller wobbles after falling ill on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'sick' an illness abroad; 'during' is the container signal, putting the illness inside the time off.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacillation is wavering or indecision, a lack of steadiness of mind.

clue.text: Pretty smart? Hardly

parts.note: read as an opposite: not pretty means homely, not smart means dim, and together they make a phrase for utterly dense

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means simply and completely foolish, and its two words are opposites of pretty and smart.

clue.text: Yet it may be part of a general hospital

definitions.text: Yet it may be part of a general hospital

parts.words: Yet it may be part of a general hospital
parts.note: a soldier of the lowest rank is not a general, yet a room named for that rank can be in a general hospital

explanation.definitionFit: A hospital room for fee-paying patients, named with the word for the lowest military rank.

clue.text: Diana's answer — divorce

parts.note: Di is the short form of Diana, so Diana's gives Di's
a solution is an answer to a problem

explanation.surface: Princess Diana's way out was a divorce.
explanation.walkthrough: DI'S, with the apostrophe dropped, then SOLUTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissolution is the formal ending of a marriage or partnership, as in a divorce.

clue.text: He knows his actions mean the high jump

definitions.text: He knows his actions mean the high jump

parts.words: He knows his actions mean the high jump
parts.note: the high jump usually means punishment, but here it is a literal leap from an aircraft

explanation.definitionFit: A soldier trained to drop by parachute from aircraft makes a very high jump.

clue.text: Port that's a credit to the East

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit; that the port's letters also run through 'a credit' is a coincidence, not a hiding device
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A harbour town is said to bring honour to the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: A, then CR, then E; Acre is a historic port in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre (Akko) is an ancient harbour city on the coast of northern Israel.

clue.text: City where mail goes astray

indicators.note: something going astray wanders off course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Post gets lost in a certain city.
explanation.definitionFit: Lima is the capital city of Peru.

clue.text: A driven out intruder

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An intruder has been forced out.
explanation.definitionFit: An invader enters territory by force, so is an intruder.

clue.text: Come up to stretch between bends

definitions.meaning: arrive at or attain, as in getting to a target
a straight section of a river between two bends

explanation.definitionFit: To reach is to arrive at something, and a reach is a straight stretch of river.

clue.text: Is a good man able to get a game?

parts.note: can means is able to
ST is the abbreviation for saint, a good man

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a virtuous man is allowed to join a game.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN, A, ST and A in turn; ST for saint is a standard crossword shortening.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a card game of the rummy family played with two packs.

clue.text: The best stuff available around the East

indicators.note: around means the word for stuff is wrapped about the compass letter

parts.note: to cram is to stuff something full
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: The finest goods on offer in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts CRAM about E; 'available' carries no letters and only pads the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of something is its finest part, as in the cream of the crop.

clue.text: Raises bucks

definitions.meaning: brings up, as of children or animals
a horse that bucks or rises up on its hind legs

explanation.definitionFit: To rear is to bring up young, and a horse rears when it rises on its hind legs.

clue.text: Not quick or not quick enough

definitions.meaning: quick in the old sense of alive, so not quick means dead

explanation.definitionFit: Late means deceased, the opposite of quick as in the quick and the dead, and also tardy.

clue.text: But it's no aspersion on the score

definitions.text: But it's no aspersion on the score

parts.words: But it's no aspersion on the score
parts.note: an aspersion is a slight on someone, but in a musical score the same word is a curved mark linking notes

explanation.definitionFit: A slur is both an insult and a curved mark in music joining notes to be played smoothly.

clue.text: Refuse to fight

definitions.meaning: rubbish, waste to be thrown out, the noun sense

explanation.definitionFit: Scrap means waste material and also a short fight.

clue.text: Rock band

parts.note: not a group of musicians but a layer within rock

explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a layer, or band, of sedimentary rock.

clue.text: Artist's bowtie?

definitions.meaning: a person who makes pictures, with the 's standing for is
a rope at the bow of a boat used to tie it up

explanation.definitionFit: A painter is an artist and also a mooring line fixed to a boat's bow.

clue.text: Bank has a way to avoid a row

definitions.text: Bank has a way to avoid a row

parts.words: Bank has a way to avoid a row
parts.note: a river bank carries a path along which horses haul boats, so nobody has to use oars

explanation.definitionFit: The path beside a canal or river used by horses hauling boats, so the bank holds a way.

clue.text: Musician having ear most developed

indicators.note: developed means the letters are worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A musician with an unusually fine ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician, especially a conductor.

clue.text: Sounds just a matter of time for us

indicators.note: sounds signals that the spoken form of a time word is wanted

parts.note: hours are units by which time is measured

explanation.surface: It is only a matter of time before something comes to us.
explanation.walkthrough: HOURS, with a silent H, is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is for us belongs to us, which is the possessive pronoun.

clue.text: An Innuit is likely to see one close up

definitions.text: An Innuit is likely to see one
definitions.meaning: an Arctic marine mammal familiar to Inuit hunters
to shut tight, as with an envelope

explanation.definitionFit: A seal is an Arctic sea mammal, and to seal is to close something securely.

clue.text: Was aware of a novel sound

indicators.note: sound tells us the word is the same when spoken as one meaning novel

parts.note: new means novel or fresh

explanation.surface: Someone was aware of a fresh noise.
explanation.walkthrough: NEW and the answer are pronounced alike, the K being silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Knew is the past tense of know, meaning was aware of.

clue.text: Pointless emotion

definitions.meaning: having no points, a score of zero in tennis

explanation.definitionFit: Love is a nil score in tennis and also a strong feeling of affection.

clue.text: See award for natural feature of Scotland

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award

explanation.surface: An onlooker notices a prize for something Scottish.
explanation.walkthrough: LO plus CH; the CH (Companion of Honour) is a British order given for service.
explanation.definitionFit: A loch is a Scottish lake or sea inlet, a natural landscape feature.

clue.text: The object of travel

parts.note: the place a journey aims to reach, read as the goal of a trip

explanation.definitionFit: A destination is the place to which someone travels, the point of the journey.

clue.text: By law mother might be culpable

indicators.note: might be signals the letters could be arranged into something else

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Under the law, a mother could be held responsible.
explanation.definitionFit: Blameworthy means deserving blame, which is what culpable means.
